mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% signals a strong accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the markets and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 1%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE increases by more than 0.5pp.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 5% month-over-month signals a weakening consumer demand, which negatively impacts corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when RSAFS drops by more than 5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening economy, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO increases for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 6% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) decrease by more than 100,000 in a month, it signals a significant labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE > 6% and PAYEMS decreases by more than 100,000.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST increases for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure and potential monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 3% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter signals robust economic growth, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, especially during an economic expansion regime.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when GDPC1 increases by more than 2% QoQ during an economic expansion.
